record.name: Mirjana Jeremić
record.title: Associate Professor
record.department: Department of Civil Engineering and Geodesy
fields: Remote Sensing and Non-Destructive Subsurface Investigation
record.bio: Mirjana Jeremić received her Diploma Engineer degree in Geodesy from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2004, and her PhD in Civil Engineering and Geodesy from the same institution in 2012. She joined the Department of Civil Engineering and Geodesy as a Teaching Assistant in 2005 and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. Her research group focuses on locating and mapping buried utilities using ground-penetrating radar, GNSS and total-station surveying, and the integration of survey results into GIS-based utility cadastres for water, gas, and electricity distribution networks. She teaches courses in Engineering Geodesy and Geoinformation Systems. The group uses a GSSI SIR-4000 GPR system, Leica TS16 total stations, and ArcGIS and QGIS environments for cadastre compilation.
open_to: contract research – GPR surveys and utility cadastre construction for infrastructure projects
consulting – subsurface utility engineering methodology and regulatory compliance
joint projects – smart city underground asset management, cross-border spatial data harmonisation
industrial PhD supervision – candidates with engineering or geomatics background
student internships – geodesy and GIS students, minimum 3-month placements
equipment access – GSSI SIR-4000 GPR system available for joint surveys under formal agreement
record.industry_experience: Jeremić has provided technical consulting on GPR survey design and utility cadastre specification to two regional distribution operators and one municipal public utility company since 2016. She served as expert reviewer for the geodetic component of a 14 km underground cable project in Srem between 2020 and 2021.
record.notes: Prefers industry partners who can provide genuine access to operational network records, as anonymised or aggregated data limits research depth. Currently supervising two doctoral candidates; capacity for a third industrial PhD candidate exists from mid-2025 onward.
